newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse lower, Dow weighs.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse lower, Dow weighs.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade lower on Friday, with weakness on Wall Street and Japan's Nikkei index pulling the market down.
Traders said the market was undergoing an expected consolidation after reaching record highs in the last few weeks, but said the longer-term outlook was still positive.
"We're still on an upward trend. There's no reason to panic, because the fundamentals are still excellent," said one dealer.
"Most things are just adjusting to the level on Wall Street," said one trader. The Dow Jones index closed trade below the crucial level of 6,000 points at 5,992.48.
Engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG was the morning's main loser, falling almost 14 percent, or 6.20 marks to 39 marks amid insolvency speculation.
But the stock recovered somewhat from an all-time low of 30 marks hit in electronic trade after the firm said the rumours were completely unfounded.
Bayerische Vereinsbank AG was firmer than the market trend after it announced nine month figures in line with expectations. The stock was up three pfennigs at 56.30 marks.

Registered shares in German reinsurance group Munich Re (Muenchener Rueckversicherung AG) gained almost five percent, climbing 155 marks to 3635 marks, on positive dividend news announced on Thursday after the bourse close.
Munich Re said its dividend for the 1995/96 business year would be 16 marks per share, against 13.5 marks last year. It also said earnings per share had more than doubled to 140 marks per share.
